title: Image evidence: Early Woodland cave explorers of the Mammoth Cave area (about 1000–200 BCE)
seoTitle: Early Woodland cavers image evidence: research notes
summary: People who explored miles into Mammoth and Salts caves to mine gypsum, leaving slippers, cane torches and gourds preserved by the dry cave air. Lost John, a miner trapped under a boulder, was found in 1935.

items.text: A preserved adult male miner ('Lost John') was found under a fallen boulder about 2.5 miles into Mammoth Cave; his remains were later removed from display and returned. Avoid depicting human remains.

Woven fiber slippers/sandals, including ones of rattlesnake master fiber; cane baskets.
[Speculative] Upper-body clothing is not documented in these sources; light woven or hide garments are an inference.
[Speculative] None documented in these sources; leave out.
Bundled river-cane torches, mussel-shell scrapers and limestone hammerstones for mining, gourd and squash containers, wooden climbing poles.

Deep dry limestone passages of the Mammoth Cave system in south-central Kentucky; cross-hatched and spiral charcoal pictographs on walls; visits in late spring–summer and late fall–winter; diet included cultivated sunflower, squash and gourd.

Inside a vast dark limestone passage, one or two cavers in fiber slippers lit by a bundled cane torch, scraping white gypsum crust into a gourd with a mussel shell. Torch-orange light against gray rock, a faint charcoal geometric design on the wall; no remains shown.
